payer_policy.§1 Scope: Advanced imaging of the lumbar spine: MRI without contrast (CPT 72148), MRI with contrast (CPT 72149), MRI without and with contrast (CPT 72158).
payer_policy.§2.1 Criteria: Prior authorization is approved when ALL of the following are documented: (a) low back pain or radicular symptoms; (b) completion of a course of supervised conservative therapy (physical therapy or chiropractic care) without adequate improvement; (c) the imaging result is expected to change management, for example surgical or injection planning.
payer_policy.§2.2 Exception: Criterion (b) is waived when the request documents a red-flag indication: suspected cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor deficit, suspected malignancy, suspected infection, or recent significant trauma.
payer_policy.§3 Documentation: Requests missing required documentation are pended for 14 calendar days; if the documentation is not received, the request is administratively denied. An administrative denial is not a medical-necessity denial.
payer_policy.§4 Contrast: Contrast studies (72149, 72158) additionally require a documented reason for contrast, such as prior lumbar spine surgery.
payer_policy.§5 Turnaround: Standard requests are decided in 7 calendar days; urgent requests in 72 hours. Scheduling holds do not make a request urgent.
payer_policy.§6 Site of service: Freestanding imaging centers are the preferred site; hospital outpatient departments require a separate site-of-care review.

formulary_policy.§3 Exceptions: Step therapy is bypassed when (a) a preferred alternative is contraindicated per prescriber attestation; (b) the member trialed the alternatives under a previous plan and this is documented by pharmacy claims or chart notes; or (c) the member is new to the plan, has been stable on the requested drug, and is requesting continuity of care. Exception (c) grants a one-time transition fill only; ongoing approval still needs §2 or exception (a) or (b).
formulary_policy.§4 Approval duration: Approvals under §2, §3(a) or §3(b) are valid for 12 months. Transition fills under §3(c) are a single 30-day supply.
formulary_policy.§5 Documentation: Chart notes or pharmacy claim history must be attached; a statement in the request form alone is insufficient.
formulary_policy.§6 Quantity: Quantity is limited to one tablet daily for the 150 mg strength.

practice_policy.title: Harbor Point Pediatrics & Family Care, Patient Attendance Policy (rev. 2026-01)
practice_policy.§5.1: Patients with three or more no-shows in a rolling 12-month period may be discharged from the practice after a written warning letter has been sent following the second no-show.
practice_policy.§5.2: Appointments that the practice cancelled, rescheduled or could not keep (clinic closure, provider illness, scheduling error) are never counted as no-shows, even if the system shows a no-show code.
practice_policy.§5.3: Exception: patients in an active course of treatment where discharge would interrupt care (for example, prenatal care, active chemotherapy coordination, post-operative follow-up) are not discharged; the case is referred to the medical director instead.
practice_policy.§5.4: Discharge letters must give 30 days of emergency coverage and a list of alternative practices.
practice_policy.§5.5: Discharge decisions are recorded in the patient's administrative record, not the clinical record.
practice_policy.§5.6: Telehealth visits missed because of a documented platform outage are treated as practice-side cancellations.

payer_policy.id: Evergreen Mutual SOC-INF-02, Site of Care for Specialty Infusions (rev. 2026-04)
payer_policy.§1 Scope: Applies to the specialty infusion drugs on Appendix A, including Tralumab (billed under J3590, unclassified biologic).
payer_policy.§2 Preferred sites: Home infusion and in-network ambulatory infusion centers (AIC) are the preferred sites of care. Physician-office infusion is also acceptable.
payer_policy.§3 Hospital outpatient (HOPD): Infusion in a hospital outpatient department is approved only when at least one of the following is documented: (a) the dose is the member's first dose, or the first dose after a gap in therapy of six months or more; (b) the member has had a moderate or severe infusion reaction to the drug that required intervention; (c) the prescriber documents a clinical condition requiring hospital-level monitoring during infusion; (d) the plan's network services team confirms that no preferred site can serve the member.
payer_policy.§4 Transition: Members already receiving HOPD infusions when this policy took effect received a one-time transition period; that transition period has closed for all members.
payer_policy.§5 Member preference: Member or prescriber convenience, proximity, or preference is not a basis for HOPD approval.
payer_policy.§6 Documentation: Infusion nursing records or ED records documenting any reaction must be attached; a prescriber's summary alone is not sufficient for §3(b).
payer_policy.§7 Duration: HOPD approvals under §3(b) or §3(c) are valid for six months, after which the reviewer reassesses whether a preferred site has become appropriate.
payer_policy.§8 Appeals: A denial of the requested site does not deny the drug; the drug remains approved at a preferred site.

(a) Standard accounts: the caller must correctly answer two of: employee ID, manager's name, last four digits of the mobile number on file. We have a mass spectrometer whose control PC runs an old operating system that the instrument vendor still requires - they say that if we patch or upgrade it, they will void the service contract, and the acquisition software only runs on that version. What I'd like is to connect the instrument PC to the network so it can push raw files to the research data storage, which then syncs to the LIMS. The vendor says they need remote access to the PC twice a year for calibration as well. I spoke to someone in Research Computing who said this is 'a security thing' and to ask the service desk. I'm happy to fill in whatever forms are needed, I just need to know who owns this and roughly how long it will take. Our instrument is booked solid for the next month, so every day we can't move data the backlog grows. Also, unrelated, the label printer in C2.14 has been printing faint labels for a week. Thanks, Dr Leonie Hartmann

RFP-2026-044 Managed Security Services - Evaluation summary (v1, 11 Sep)

Three compliant bids were received: Ironbark Cyber, Brightline Secure and Cobalt Watch. All three passed the mandatory requirements (24x7 SOC, EU data residency, named service manager). Weighted scoring (technical 50%, commercial 30%, references 20%) placed Brightline Secure first, Cobalt Watch second and Ironbark Cyber third. Brightline's technical response was the strongest, particularly its threat-hunting methodology and onboarding plan, and its price was the lowest of the three. Ironbark's price was the highest and its response relied heavily on subcontractors for out-of-hours coverage.

Recommendation (v1): award to Brightline Secure, subject to satisfactory reference checks, which were outstanding at the time of writing.

Prepared by: Anneke Voss, Category Manager, IT Services

Reference checks have now been completed. Two of Brightline Secure's three references reported missed escalations during major incidents in the last year, and one said it had terminated its contract early for that reason. Cobalt Watch's three references were all positive, including one from a regulated financial services client. Ironbark Cyber's references were mixed. The references criterion has been rescored accordingly. Brightline Secure now ranks second overall and Cobalt Watch first. Commercial scores are unchanged: Brightline Secure remains the lowest price.

Revised recommendation: award to Cobalt Watch. Brightline Secure to be informed that it was unsuccessful on references. The recommendation from v1 is withdrawn.

Prepared by: Anneke Voss, Category Manager, IT Services

state.legal_review_memo:
PRIVILEGED - LEGAL REVIEW MEMO
To: Procurement (IT Services category)
From: Commercial Legal (A. Mensah)
Re: Kitefin Logistics Software - Master Services Agreement, vendor redlines of 16 Sep

1. Summary
Kitefin returned our MSA template with seven redlines. Two are acceptable, four need to go back to the vendor, and one needs escalation to the Legal Director before we can respond. Nothing in the redlines touches the data processing agreement, which Kitefin accepted in full.

2. Clause-by-clause
2.1 Limitation of liability (cl. 12.1). Our template caps each party's liability at the fees paid in the prior 12 months. Kitefin proposes 6 months. The playbook fallback allows nothing below 12 months for systems that run operational processes, and this platform will run warehouse dispatch. Push back.
2.2 IP indemnity (cl. 13). Kitefin accepted our standard wording. No action.
2.3 Renewal (cl. 15.2). Our template renews for 12-month terms. Kitefin proposes 24-month renewal terms. The playbook fallback allows only 12-month renewal terms. Push back.
2.4 Payment terms (cl. 8.3). Our template is net 45. Kitefin proposes net 30. The playbook allows net 30 for suppliers that qualify as SMEs under our supplier definition. Kitefin's account director confirmed by email that Kitefin qualifies as an SME; we have not seen accounts. Accept, on that basis.
2.5 Audit rights (cl. 17). Our template allows audits on reasonable notice. The playbook fallback allows limiting audits to once per year, provided an additional audit is always permitted after a security incident. Kitefin's version limits audits to once per year and deletes the post-incident audit. Push back and reinstate the incident audit.
2.6 Governing law (cl. 24). Kitefin proposes its home jurisdiction. The playbook requires our governing law unless the Legal Director approves otherwise; I do not recommend asking for that here. Push back.
2.7 Termination for convenience (cl. 16.3). Kitefin deleted our right to terminate for convenience entirely. There is no playbook fallback for this clause; removal is outside my authority to accept. Escalate to the Legal Director before any response goes to Kitefin.

3. Recommendation
Accept 2.2 and 2.4. Send 2.1, 2.3, 2.5 and 2.6 back with our fallback positions. Hold the response until the Legal Director has considered 2.7. Please do not share this memo with the vendor.

A. Mensah, Senior Commercial Counsel

Q1. Do you publish a modern slavery or forced labour statement?
A1. Yes, published annually on our website and signed by our managing director.

Q2. How do you audit your own factories?
A2. Our two garment factories are audited annually by an accredited third-party social compliance auditor. The latest audits found minor findings on fire exit signage, since closed.

Q3. How do you assess your own suppliers (tier 2, e.g. fabric mills and dye houses)?
A3. Tier 2 suppliers complete our self-assessment questionnaire every two years. We do not currently audit tier 2 sites.

Q4. Do workers pay any fees to obtain employment?
A4. We do not charge workers recruitment fees. Some of the labour agents we use for seasonal staff charge workers a registration fee; we are phasing these agents out over the next two seasons.

Q5. Do you hold workers' identity documents?
A5. No. Workers keep their own documents; lockers are provided.

Q6. What are your working-hours practices?
A6. Overtime is voluntary and capped in line with local law. During peak season some lines exceed the legal cap with the written consent of workers, and all overtime is paid at premium rates.

Q7. Do you have a grievance mechanism?
A7. Yes, an anonymous hotline in the three main languages spoken by our workers, run by an external provider.

Q8. Have you had to remediate any forced labour or child labour cases?
A8. No remediation has been required to date.

Q9. Do you subcontract production?
A9. Only embroidery, to two approved subcontractors listed in our supplier register.

Q10. How are wages paid?
A10. Monthly, by bank transfer, with itemised payslips. Seasonal staff recruited through agents are paid by the agent, who deducts accommodation where workers use agent-provided housing.

A11. We do not operate dormitories. Some agent-recruited seasonal staff live in housing arranged by the agents; we have not inspected it.

A12. Summary reports are available on request under NDA.

Q13. Do you audit or monitor your labour agents?
A13. Agents sign our code of conduct when appointed. We have not audited them; we rely on worker feedback through the hotline, which has received no complaints about agents this year.

A14. We are working towards an industry sustainability certification next year.

ENHANCED DUE DILIGENCE REPORT - Coastline Port Services SARL
Prepared for: Group Procurement, Port Logistics category
Purpose: proposed three-year contract for stevedoring and customs brokerage at the Port of Selmar (Republic of Veltria).

1. Corporate profile. Coastline Port Services SARL is a privately held company incorporated in Veltria in 2012, with around 180 employees. Registered shareholders: Yusuf Karan (70%) and Coastline Holdings Ltd (30%), a holding company in the Kingdom of Morland whose sole shareholder is also Yusuf Karan. Directors: Yusuf Karan (managing director) and Leyla Karan.

2. Politically exposed persons. Leyla Karan, a director, is the spouse of Emre Karan, the current Deputy Minister of Transport of Veltria, whose ministry oversees port concessions and licenses customs brokers. Leyla Karan has held her directorship since 2015, before her husband's appointment in 2023. No other PEP connections were identified.

3. Sanctions. Company, shareholders and directors were screened against the synthetic consolidated lists used by the Group; no matches.

4. Adverse media. No adverse media on the company or its directors was found in English, French or local-language sources covering the last ten years. One 2021 trade press article praised the company's safety record.

5. Contract context. The contract would require the vendor to obtain port access permits and customs brokerage licences from authorities under the Ministry of Transport. The Group would be the largest customer of the vendor.

6. Financial overview. Filed accounts for the last three years show steady revenue growth and modest profits. The auditor's opinions were unqualified. The company has no outstanding tax disputes on the public record.

7. References. Two current customers (a regional shipping line and a fruit importer) described the company as reliable and well connected at the port. One said the company 'always gets permits through quickly', which the analyst notes could reflect efficiency or influence and should be explored in interviews.

8. Analyst assessment. The PEP connection is significant given the ministry's direct role in licensing the services being purchased. There is no indication of wrongdoing. Recommended mitigations: anti-bribery contractual clauses with audit rights, a certification that no payments are made to public officials, and annual refresh of this report. Senior management approval is required under the Group's third-party policy for any vendor with a PEP connection in a role relevant to the contract.

9. Next steps. Interviews with the managing director and Leyla Karan are proposed before contract award, covering how permits are obtained, any contact with the Ministry, and whether Leyla Karan would step back from government-facing work during the contract.

MINUTES - Tender Panel, RFP-2026-048 Facilities Management (Northern sites)
Present: H. Okoye (Chair, Procurement), R. Singh (Facilities), M. Duarte (Finance), P. Kowalczyk (Health & Safety), L. Brennan (Estates)

1. Declarations of interest. None declared at the start of the meeting. The Chair reminded members that interests arising during the meeting must be declared immediately.

2. Technical scores. The panel reviewed the moderated technical scores. Brightstone FM ranked first on technical quality, Harwell Services second and Ostara Facilities third. P. Kowalczyk noted that Ostara's safety method statements were the weakest of the three and would need significant work before mobilisation. L. Brennan commented that Harwell's estates maintenance approach was 'the most practical of the three' and argued for raising its moderated score on question 4; the panel agreed a one-point increase. R. Singh noted that Brightstone's staffing model was the most resilient, with named relief staff at every site.

3. Commercial scores. M. Duarte presented the commercial evaluation. Ostara was the lowest price, Harwell second and Brightstone the most expensive. Combined weighted scores placed Harwell first overall, Brightstone a close second and Ostara third. M. Duarte observed that the margin between the top two was narrow enough that small scoring changes could reverse it.

4. Declaration during the meeting. During the discussion of Harwell's mobilisation plan, L. Brennan declared that her former line manager is now Harwell's regional director and that they remain in regular contact socially. The Chair asked L. Brennan to leave the meeting for the remainder of the Harwell discussion and the recommendation vote. L. Brennan left the meeting.

5. Recommendation. The remaining members voted on the recommendation. H. Okoye, M. Duarte and P. Kowalczyk supported an award to Harwell Services. R. Singh preferred Brightstone FM, citing its stronger technical score and his concern about Harwell's staffing levels at the two largest sites, and asked for his dissent to be minuted. The Chair confirmed the panel remained quorate after L. Brennan's departure.

6. Actions. Procurement to update the conflicts register with L. Brennan's declaration; Procurement to prepare the award recommendation report for the Category Board; R. Singh's concerns about staffing to be raised with Harwell at clarification.

7. Any other business. None.

Minutes approved by: H. Okoye (Chair)

TENDER EVALUATION REPORT - RFP-2026-071 Office Cleaning Services (Leeds, Harlow and Bristol sites)
Prepared by: Category Manager, Facilities | Status: Final draft for Category Board

1. Background
The current cleaning contract expires at the end of the year. The tender was advertised openly and three bids were received: Sparkline Facilities, Brightside Cleaning Co. and Evergreen Hygiene Services. The contract covers daily office cleaning, periodic deep cleans, washroom consumables and a reactive call-out service at all three sites for an initial three-year term with an option to extend by two years.

2. Mandatory checks
All three bidders submitted the required forms. Evergreen Hygiene Services did not provide the mandatory public liability insurance certificate by the clarification deadline and was therefore excluded from further evaluation. Sparkline and Brightside passed all mandatory checks, including the living-wage declaration and the modern slavery statement check.

3. Quality evaluation (60%)
Brightside scored higher on quality. Its mobilisation plan was the most detailed of the bids, with named site supervisors for each location and a clear plan for the Harlow night shift. Its approach to consumables and eco-certified chemicals was also stronger, and it proposed a monthly quality audit with photographs shared with our facilities team. Sparkline's response was competent but more generic; the panel noted that its staffing plan for Harlow relied on agency staff for the first three months and that its quality audit proposal was quarterly rather than monthly.

4. Price evaluation (40%)
Sparkline submitted the lowest price. Brightside's price was higher but within the approved budget. Evergreen's price was not evaluated. Both remaining bidders priced consumables on an open-book basis.

5. Social value
Both remaining bidders committed to paying at least the regional living wage. Brightside additionally offered two apprenticeships per year and a commitment to recruit locally at Harlow.

6. Risks
The financial check on Sparkline returned an amber rating because of losses in the last reported year. Sparkline has also recently lost two large contracts in the region. Brightside's financial check was green. Neither bidder has had a reportable health and safety incident in the last three years according to their declarations.

7. Combined scores and recommendation
On the combined weighted score Brightside ranks first and Sparkline a close second. On balance the panel recommends an award to Brightside Cleaning Co. The panel noted that Sparkline would also be an acceptable award if Finance were comfortable with its amber financial rating, and that the price difference between the two bids is modest. The final decision rests with the Category Board.

Appendix A - Finance note (added after the panel meeting): Finance has reviewed Sparkline's latest accounts. The amber rating reflects one-off restructuring costs and we are comfortable with Sparkline's financial position for a contract of this size.

Appendix B - Facilities Director comment: I would still prefer Brightside for the Harlow night shift given the agency staffing concern in Sparkline's bid.

Appendix C - Procurement note: The Category Board meets on the 30th. If the Board chooses Sparkline on price, the award report must record why the quality gap was judged acceptable.

Morland Business Daily - 14 August 2026

PORT HAULIER UNDER INVESTIGATION OVER DRIVER PAY

The Morland Labour Inspectorate has opened an investigation into Ridgeway Haulage over allegations that agency drivers were required to repay 'training and uniform costs' from their wages and had their passports held by a labour agency while working on port contracts. The inspectorate confirmed it had received complaints from three drivers and had visited the company's depot at Selmar Docks. No findings have been published.

One of the drivers, who asked not to be named, told this newspaper that he had worked six-day weeks for four months and that deductions left him with less than he had been promised when he was recruited abroad. He said he had asked for his passport back twice before it was returned. The newspaper was unable to verify his account independently.

Ridgeway Haulage said in a statement that it 'does not tolerate any form of labour exploitation', that the drivers concerned were employed by an independent agency, Quayside Staffing, and that it had suspended its use of that agency pending the outcome. The company added that it had commissioned an external review of all labour agencies it uses and would publish a summary of the findings.

The company, founded in 2008, operates around 120 trucks from depots in Selmar and Port Allen and counts several large retailers among its customers. It should not be confused with Ridgeway Freight Forwarding, an unrelated company based in the capital, or with Ridgeway Logistics UK, a separately owned firm with a similar name.

Quayside Staffing did not respond to requests for comment. Labour rights groups said the allegations, if proven, would amount to indicators of forced labour under international standards, citing the retention of identity documents and deductions for recruitment-related costs. A spokesperson for the Morland Hauliers Association said the sector relies heavily on agency drivers during peak season and that members had been reminded of their obligations to check agency practices.

Two of Ridgeway's retail customers told this newspaper they were 'monitoring the situation' and had asked the company for details of its agency checks. Neither said it would suspend its contract.

The inspectorate said its investigation would take several months and that it could not comment on individual cases.

[Screening context added by analyst: vendor under review is 'Ridgeway Haulage Ltd', company number MRL-30887, depots Selmar and Port Allen. Our contract would cover container haulage from Selmar Docks, using a mix of employed and agency drivers.]

vendor_risk_assessment.service: On-site maintenance of retail store refrigeration and HVAC across 140 stores
vendor_risk_assessment.data_access: Store managers' names and phone numbers; access to a work-order portal. No customer data, no payment systems.
vendor_risk_assessment.system_access: Read/write access to the work-order portal only; no network access in stores; engineers use their own tablets on a guest network.
vendor_risk_assessment.physical_access: Engineers attend stores unaccompanied, including back-of-house and plant rooms, often outside trading hours. Store keys are held in lockboxes whose codes are shared with Lumen's dispatch team.
vendor_risk_assessment.subcontracting: Uses regional subcontractors for about a third of visits; subcontractor vetting is 'in line with Lumen policy', not independently reviewed.
vendor_risk_assessment.health_and_safety: Two reportable refrigerant leaks in the last year at other customers' sites; F-gas certification current for all directly employed engineers; subcontractor certification not evidenced. One of the two leaks caused a store evacuation.
vendor_risk_assessment.business_continuity: Documented plan; national coverage via three regional hubs.
vendor_risk_assessment.concentration: Sole provider for refrigeration maintenance across the estate. Food safety depends on chiller uptime; a failed chiller forces stock disposal under the food safety policy.
vendor_risk_assessment.previous_assessment: Two years ago: Tier 2, no findings. At that time Lumen did not use subcontractors.
vendor_risk_assessment.tiering_rules: Tier 1 (low): no data, no physical access, non-critical. Tier 2 (medium): limited personal data or unaccompanied physical access or operational dependency. Tier 3 (high): sensitive data or privileged system access, or safety-critical work with unverified subcontracting, or sole provider of a critical service. The highest applicable tier applies.
vendor_risk_assessment.assessor_comment: Draft rating Tier 2, carried over from the previous assessment. Data and system risk are low. I have flagged the subcontractor certification gap for follow-up.
vendor_risk_assessment.store_operations_feedback: Regional operations managers report that response times are good and engineers are generally well regarded. Two stores reported subcontracted engineers arriving without ID badges; one store manager refused entry until Lumen dispatch confirmed the booking by phone.
vendor_risk_assessment.food_safety_note: From the Food Safety Lead: 'Refrigeration is a critical control point for us. Any contractor working on chillers must be competent and certified, and we need to know who is on site.'

state.renewal_memo_v1:
CONTRACT RENEWAL MEMO - Document Management Platform (Fernwood Software)
Prepared by: Category Manager, IT Software, 2 Sep

The current contract ends in the first quarter of next year. Options considered: (A) renew with Fernwood for two years at the renewal price offered; (B) run a competitive tender and migrate to a new platform; (C) renew for one year only and tender during that year.

Performance: Fernwood met its availability targets in eleven of the last twelve months. User satisfaction is moderate; the main complaints concern search speed and the mobile app. Two P1 incidents occurred in the year, both resolved within SLA. Fernwood's account management has been responsive, and its product roadmap includes a new search engine next year, although roadmap dates have slipped before.

Price: Fernwood has offered a renewal price increase in line with the published index plus the contractual maximum uplift. Market benchmarking suggests two competitors could offer comparable functionality at a lower annual cost, but migration would require an estimated six months of project effort and a data migration of roughly 40 million documents.

Risks: Option B carries migration risk during the finance system upgrade planned for the same period. Option A locks in two years at a price above market. Option C keeps flexibility but Fernwood's one-year price is higher than its two-year price.

Stakeholders: Legal and Records Management rely on Fernwood's retention and legal-hold features and asked that any replacement match them before migration. IT Architecture prefers to consolidate onto a platform that integrates with the new finance system.

Recommendation (v1): Option A - renew for two years, to avoid migration risk during the finance system upgrade.
state.cfo_comment: CFO, 10 Sep: I don't want a two-year lock-in above market. The finance system upgrade has been moved out by a year, so migration clashes are less of a concern. Please revisit.
state.renewal_memo_v2_addendum: Addendum, 15 Sep: Following the CFO's comment and the revised finance programme timetable, the recommendation is changed to Option C - renew for one year and run a competitive tender during that year, with the aim of migrating after the finance upgrade is complete. The higher one-year price is accepted as the cost of flexibility. Option B (tender now) remains the second choice if Fernwood will not offer a one-year renewal. Records Management's retention and legal-hold requirements will be mandatory in the tender specification.
